mu_name_from: VersionSeasonSix/Items/Orbs.cs:43 -- MU's own number, our level
why_this_one:
The route a knight learns a skill by (docs/skills-dk.md SS3.3): bought or found, read once, and the skill is his for good. Until this row existed the skills were handed over at the character's level, which was a stand-in for exactly this item.

Its number in group 12 is MU own.

Its level and drop level are 44, which is VersionSeasonSix/Items/Orbs.cs:43 -- MU's own number, our level.
mesh_note: No geometry of its own. Gem01.bmd through Gem05.bmd are byte-identical in MuMain's Data/Item -- one md5 across all five -- so every orb in MU is one model told apart by its row, and this names the one the pipeline has built.

stats.note: An orb has no damage roll and no hand: it is a Prize and nothing else, and the shape of the row is the elf orbs' own (Version075/Items/Orbs.cs:63-67) -- one cell, durability one, dropped by monsters.
stats.durability_note: One. One reading, as a scroll is.
stats.classes_from: CharacterClasses.DarkKnight. Every skill in this orb's family is a knight's; Prize.ReadBy refuses the other two whatever their level.
stats.requires_note: What the character must BE to read it. Carried raw: docs/mu-scrolls-and-orbs.md SS4 establishes that a non-wearable row's requirement is used verbatim rather than run through `(3 x drop level x raw / 100) + 20`, and sim/items.cpp's `asks` already takes `need_level` unscaled. The same number is on the skill block below, which is what Realm::useItem checks -- the two must agree, and a row where they do not is a transcription error caught for free.

skill.note: What the orb teaches. Read once and gone -- the durability of one is what 'used once' means on this row.
skill.name: Rageful Blow
skill.tells: The weapon driven down into the ground, and what it breaks is the three tiles ahead of him.
skill.tells_from: The skill's own line in sim/skills.cpp, kept letter for letter so the orb's tooltip and the skill's card cannot say different things about the same blow. MU never prints a line like this at all; it is ours, as it is on the elf's orbs.
skill.energy_from: None. The knight's skills carry no energy requirement in 0.75 -- CreateSkill is called with mana and nothing else for all six (Version075/SkillsInitializer.cs:58-63) -- and gating them behind the stats that make them good would charge twice (docs/skills-dk.md SS3.3).
